title: Merchant: webhooks not arriving since last night

customer.name: Bayo Ogunleye (Engineering Lead, Kaduna Fresh Foods e-commerce)
rails: Card + bank transfer checkout, webhook-driven order fulfillment
customer.account_summary: Merchant integration live 11 months, ~4,000 orders/month, webhook-dependent order confirmation flow.

messages.text: Since last night our orders are not being marked as paid in our system, but your merchant dashboard shows the payments as succeeded. This is causing real problems — customers are paying but not getting their order confirmations and our warehouse team isn't releasing shipments. Please check urgently, this is a B2B outage for us.
We haven't changed anything on our end recently. Is this an outage on your side?

hidden_root_cause: The merchant's own infrastructure team rotated their server's TLS certificate at 22:10 the previous night, but the new certificate chain was installed without the required intermediate CA certificate. Our webhook sender performs full chain validation and now receives SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILED on every delivery attempt to the merchant's endpoint. Retries are continuing on the standard 24-hour exponential backoff schedule (window opened 22:14 the previous night and closes 22:14 that night, roughly 13 hours after this ticket was raised), so the merchant has received zero of the 47 queued webhook notifications so far, even though the underlying payments are succeeding correctly on our side. Once the 24h window closes, no further automatic retries will happen — a manual replay after the merchant fixes the cert chain is required regardless.
red_herring: The merchant states 'we haven't changed anything recently' and asks if it's our outage — this points suspicion at us, but Processor & Partner Status shows all systems green; the actual change (a cert rotation) may not have been visible to the person messaging us if it was done by a different sub-team overnight.

knowledge_base.title: Webhook delivery failure: TLS chain errors
knowledge_base.body: SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILED with 'unable to get local issuer certificate' means the destination server's TLS certificate chain is missing the intermediate CA. This is a merchant-side server config issue, not a payments outage. Advise the merchant to include the full certificate chain (leaf + intermediate) in their server config. Offer to replay failed webhooks for the affected window once fixed; recommend polling the Payments Status API as a stopgap.

root_cause_options.text: Merchant's TLS certificate rotation last night is missing the intermediate CA in the chain; our webhook sender fails the handshake and cannot deliver, though payments themselves are succeeding.
We are having a payments processing outage that is silently failing all transactions.
The merchant's API key was revoked, blocking all outbound communication.
Our webhook system has a bug that stopped sending events to all merchants globally.

resolution_options.text: Explain the TLS certificate chain issue is merchant-side, ask them to fix the chain (include intermediate CA), offer to replay the queued webhooks once fixed, and recommend polling the Payments Status API meanwhile.
Tell them it's likely a temporary issue on our side and to wait it out.
Manually mark all their pending orders as paid in their system on their behalf.
Regenerate their API keys as a first troubleshooting step.

customer_expectation_timeframe: Immediate diagnosis; webhook replay available as soon as merchant confirms the cert chain fix
model_reply: Hi Bayo, thanks for the detailed report — I've dug into this and can give you a clear answer. Your payments are processing successfully on our side (no outage here: Processor Status is fully green). The issue is that every webhook delivery attempt to your endpoint since 22:14 last night has failed with an SSL handshake error — specifically, the certificate chain your server is presenting is missing the intermediate CA certificate. This lines up with a TLS cert rotation timestamped last night on your endpoint, even if it wasn't visible on your side of the team. Once your infrastructure team adds the intermediate certificate to the chain (this is usually a one-line config fix, e.g. concatenating the full chain in your server config), deliveries should resume immediately. In the meantime: (1) I can replay all 47 queued webhook events for the affected window as soon as your endpoint is fixed — just confirm here and I'll trigger it, and (2) as a stopgap, you can poll our Payments Status API by order reference to confirm paid orders and release shipments without waiting on webhooks. Let me know once the cert is fixed and I'll replay immediately.
